Set up a remote Mac for development: Xcode, Homebrew and Git

Reviewed: 2026-11-21 · WodeMac

On day one, log in to the cloud Mac over remote desktop and check the macOS version. Then install the Xcode command line tools (xcode-select --install), the Xcode version your project needs, Homebrew and Git, set your Git identity and SSH key, and clone a repository to get a build and tests passing. A WodeMac Mac arrives with the WodeMac Remote Screen app and admin rights, and WodeMac helps with the first login.

First remote login

  1. Connect with WodeMac Remote Screen from a computer, phone or iPad, following the delivery instructions. WodeMac helps with the first login remotely.
  2. If you were given an initial password, change it to a strong one of your own and decide who on the team holds it.
  3. Check the macOS version in About This Mac and make sure it meets the requirements of the Xcode version you plan to install.
  4. If you want terminal access, turn on Remote Login (SSH) in System Settings › General › Sharing.

WodeMac and the hosting provider keep admin access for maintenance, so plan accounts and data with that in mind.

Install the command line tools and Xcode

Start with the Xcode command line tools, which include clang, make and Apple's git:

xcode-select --install

For iOS or macOS apps, install Xcode from the App Store with your Apple Account. Then point the tools at it, accept the license and install the first-launch components:

sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer
sudo xcodebuild -license accept
xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch
xcodebuild -version

Install Homebrew and Git

Use the install command from brew.sh:

/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"

When it finishes, the installer prints “Next steps” for adding brew to your PATH; follow them. On Apple silicon, Homebrew lives in /opt/homebrew, and you can load it in the current shell with:

eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"

Then install a current Git and set your commit identity:

brew install git
git --version
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@example.com"

Get your first project building

Generate an SSH key just for this Mac, preferably with a passphrase, and add the public key to your code host:

ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "you@example.com"
cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub

Clone a repository you are authorized to use, list its schemes, then build and test (replace MyApp and the simulator name with your project and an available device):

git clone git@github.com:your-org/your-repo.git
cd your-repo
xcodebuild -list
xcodebuild -scheme MyApp -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 16" build test

You can also open the project in Xcode and run it once in the simulator.

Before you log off

  • Write down the macOS, Xcode, Homebrew and Git versions and your setup steps.
  • Check free space in System Settings › General › Storage and remove simulator runtimes you do not need.
  • Confirm which people and devices can connect to the Mac.
  • Push your work to a remote repository; do not treat this Mac as the only copy.

FAQ

Do I have to install Xcode myself on a WodeMac Mac?

Yes. The WodeMac Remote Screen app is installed at delivery; you install Xcode, Homebrew, Git and other tools in the versions your project needs, using your admin rights.

What is the difference between xcode-select --install and Xcode?

The first installs only the command line tools, such as the compiler and git. Full Xcode adds the iOS SDK, simulators and the IDE, and you need it to build iOS apps.

Where does Homebrew install on Apple silicon?

In /opt/homebrew. Follow the Next steps the installer prints to add it to your PATH, and new terminals will find brew.

Should I use remote desktop or SSH?

Either works. WodeMac Remote Screen suits Xcode and simulator work; for command-line work you can turn on Remote Login and use SSH.
